🟤 Workshop Key Unlocked

GIS and Spatial Statistics Track

Welcome to the **GIS and Spatial Statistics Track**. It builds on the advanced visualization pages (ggplot2 modules, galleries, interactive plots, exporting) and adds a spatial toolkit: reading and mapping spatial data with `sf`, defining neighbours and spatial weights, testing for spatial autocorrelation with **Moran's I**, finding clusters with **local Moran's I (LISA)**, **Getis-Ord Gi\***, **Geary's C**, join counts and the scan statistic, and checking regression residuals for spatial structure. All examples use a synthetic district of 80 blocks with a planted hot spot, so no real boundaries or personal data are involved.

## 🎯 Workshop Goals - Read, transform and join spatial data with sf, and keep track of coordinate reference systems - Make clear static and interactive maps and choose a sensible classification - Define neighbours and spatial weights, and know how the choice changes the answer - Test for global spatial autocorrelation with Moran's I and read the Moran scatterplot - Locate clusters and outliers with local Moran's I (LISA) and hot spots with Getis-Ord Gi* - Use Geary's C, join counts and the scan statistic, and check regression residuals for spatial structure ## 📚 What This Track Covers - 📁 R Foundations & Data Wrangling - 📐 Data Visualization — grammar, best practices, ggplot2 modules 1–4 - 🖼️ Plot Gallery (basic to advanced) and Specialized & Interactive Plots - ⚙️ Exporting, Plotting Tools and Debugging - 🗺️ Spatial Data with sf, Maps and Choropleths - 🧭 Neighbours and Spatial Weights - 📍 Global Moran's I and Local Moran's I (LISA) - 🔥 Geary's C, Getis-Ord, Join Counts and the Scan Statistic - 📉 Spatial Regression and Residual Tests ## 🧭 Find Your Way Around Use the navigation bar above to browse all modules. Key starting points: - 🗺️ **[Spatial Data with sf](gis/spatial_data_sf.qmd)** — Start here: spatial objects, coordinate systems, joining attributes - 🧭 **[Neighbours and Weights](gis/spatial_weights.qmd)** — Queen, rook and k-nearest neighbours, and row-standardised weights - 📍 **[Global Moran's I](gis/morans_i.qmd)** — Is the pattern clustered? Test, permutation p-value and Moran scatterplot - 🔥 **[Local Moran's I (LISA)](gis/local_moran_lisa.qmd)** — Where are the clusters and spatial outliers? - 🎨 **[Data Visualization](data-visualization/ggplot_grammar.qmd)** — Grammar of graphics and all four ggplot2 modules > The navbar has the full visualization library as well as the spatial pages. ## 📥 Downloadable Resources All files for this track are available below, grouped by type. ### 📄 R Scripts - [Make Gis Data](gis/make_gis_data.R) ### 🗄️ Datasets - 📦 [District Blocks](data/gis/district_blocks.geojson) `.geojson` - 📊 [Facilities](data/gis/facilities.csv) `.csv` --- > 💡 **Tip:** Never mapped data in R? Read **Spatial Data with sf** and **Maps and Choropleths** first, then go straight to **Global Moran's I**.
